items.prompt: A travel agent gathers itinerary evidence and drafts reimbursement submissions; amounts above a threshold create a financial obligation and policy exceptions depend on user intent. Where should human attention occur?
constraints: Routine lookup and drafting are reversible.
High-value submission is an external side effect.
Ambiguous preferences cannot be inferred safely.

options.text: Approve every lookup and draft so reviewers see each intermediate result and can catch policy exceptions before reimbursement proceeds.
Automate lookup and drafting, ask the user to resolve intent, and require confirmation before high-value submission.
Let the agent submit from the policy prompt, then review the payment record and reverse errors.
Infer intent from prior trips, submit routine vendors, and confirm only unusual exceptions.

feedback.Reason: Human attention belongs at the intent and consequential-action boundaries, while reversible preparation can be automated.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes agents pausing for human feedback at checkpoints or blockers and asking users when preference or intent cannot be safely inferred.
Details.scenarioApplication: Gather receipts and prepare a draft automatically, pause for ambiguous preferences, and bind confirmation to the high-value reimbursement before submission.
Details.errorCorrection: Reviewing every harmless step causes fatigue, while automatic submission or historical inference can authorize the wrong financial action.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the assistant only prepared a draft with no submission capability and preferences were explicit, review could occur at the later external action.
Details.transfer: Place human review where ambiguity or consequence begins, not at every reversible intermediate step.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Per-step approval creates fatigue without protecting the consequential boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Post-submission review cannot undo an unauthorized financial obligation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Past trips are not proof of this user’s current intent or exception authorization.

items.prompt: A code agent prompts for approval before every shell command; reviewers approve nearly all prompts, including one that changes a deployment manifest after malicious pasted issue text. Routine work can run in a constrained sandbox. What should change?
constraints: The manifest change is high impact and content-influenced.
Sandbox, focused review, and injection tests are available.

options.text: Remove approval because most commands are approved, and rely on deployment monitoring to catch manifest changes.
Approve prompts faster, retain per-command review, and add a caution reminder above each action.
Sandbox routine commands, focus deployment approval on exact diff, and test injected content.
Keep per-command prompts, add a larger warning, and ask reviewers to acknowledge it before every command.

feedback.Reason: Per-command prompts create fatigue without distinguishing consequence; containment and focused, evidence-backed review protect the deployment boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes human approval as fallible under prompt fatigue and combines it with filesystem, network, and process containment.
Details.scenarioApplication: Run routine commands in a constrained environment, show the exact manifest diff and source context for deployment approval, and replay hostile issue text.
Details.errorCorrection: Removing approval loses the boundary, faster approval does not improve evidence, and more warnings preserve the same fatigue pattern.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every command were read-only inside a sandbox, per-command approval could be unnecessary while one release review still guards deployment.
Details.transfer: Use containment for routine autonomy and reserve human attention for consequential actions with clear evidence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Removing approval abandons the high-impact deployment boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Faster prompts preserve reviewer fatigue and do not expose the exact action.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A larger warning leaves command frequency and the fatigue mechanism unchanged.

items.prompt: A benefits agent can answer and check policy but may start enrollment; conflicting documents need human judgment and the reviewer must see why the agent paused. Select TWO controls.
constraints: Conflicting evidence and uncertainty are visible.
Checkpoint evidence and the eventual action can be audited.

options.text: Pause on a policy conflict or defined enrollment threshold, and show the evidence and uncertainty to the reviewer.
Ask for approval after every policy lookup so no intermediate decision is autonomous.
Let the agent enroll when its confidence is high and record only the final account state.
Record the checkpoint, human decision, and resulting enrollment action for an auditable state transition.
Continue checking documents until the conflict disappears, then enroll without a new human decision.

feedback.Reason: The agent should pause at ambiguity or the state-changing boundary, expose evidence for accountable judgment, and preserve an audit trail.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes checkpoints and blockers where agents pause for human feedback; the threshold, evidence display, and audit record are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Present the conflicting documents, policy match, and proposed enrollment action, obtain a human decision, and log the checkpoint and resulting state change.
Details.errorCorrection: Per-lookup review causes fatigue, confidence is not authorization, hiding evidence removes accountability, and continuing until conflict disappears can silently choose a policy interpretation.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If all policy documents agreed and enrollment were only a reversible draft, the agent could proceed to the later commit checkpoint.
Details.transfer: Pause when uncertainty or consequence crosses the declared boundary, and give the reviewer enough evidence to own the decision.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Reviewing every lookup creates fatigue instead of focusing attention on the conflict or state change.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Confidence does not authorize an enrollment or replace human judgment on conflicting evidence.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Silently waiting for agreement can turn a conflict into an unreviewed policy choice.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Pausing at the conflict or threshold gives the reviewer the evidence needed for a deliberate decision.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Recording the checkpoint and resulting action preserves accountable evidence for the state change.

items.prompt: A medical scheduling assistant may suggest slots and draft messages but must not infer treatment preference from an ambiguous note. What should it do?
constraints: Slot lookup and drafting are reversible.
The patient or clinician can supply the missing preference.
Sending or committing a choice can affect care.

options.text: Choose the earliest slot as a neutral default, send a draft booking request, and let the patient correct it afterward.
Infer preference from historical frequency, book the most common choice, and record the assumption.
Refuse all scheduling help until a complete treatment plan is supplied.
Prepare slots and the draft, then ask the patient or clinician to resolve preference before sending or booking.

feedback.Reason: The assistant can prepare reversible work but must pause for the person who owns intent before committing a preference-dependent action.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says agents should recognize gaps requiring user preference or intent and pause for clarification rather than act on assumptions.
Details.scenarioApplication: List eligible slots, draft the message, identify the unresolved preference, and request clarification before sending or booking.
Details.errorCorrection: Earliest-slot defaults and historical frequency invent intent, while refusing all preparation withholds useful reversible assistance.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the note explicitly named the preference and scheduling remained reversible, the assistant could choose a matching slot without a clarification pause.
Details.transfer: Preserve user autonomy by asking the intent owner when a consequential choice is under-specified, while completing safe preparation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Earliest is not a neutral preference when the note is ambiguous.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Historical frequency does not establish the patient’s current treatment intent.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A blanket refusal discards reversible preparation that does not require the missing preference.

items.prompt: An agent obtains approval to pay invoice 184 for a displayed recipient, amount, and currency. Before execution, the invoice record or exchange rate changes, but the approval remains valid in the session. What must the application do?
constraints: Approval can bind canonical parameters and an invoice version.
The current record can be read immediately before the write.
A changed recipient, amount, currency, or version is a material mutation.

options.text: Treat invoice approval as valid for the session even if recipient, amount, or currency changes before execution.
Ask for approval once per session and let the payment tool use its latest record after the original review.
Bind approval to action parameters and state version, revalidate before writing, and reapprove after mutation.
Execute the original amount, let reconciliation correct differences, and record the discrepancy afterward.

feedback.Reason: Approval authorizes the exact reviewed action and state, not an evolving intent; any material change requires fresh validation and approval.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says agents should gain ground truth from the environment, pause for human feedback at checkpoints or blockers, and use stopping conditions to maintain control; exact binding and reapproval are application controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Hash recipient, amount, currency, invoice version, and relevant policy state into the approval, re-read them before the write, and stop when any value differs.
Details.errorCorrection: Session-level intent and latest-record execution let the tool perform an action the reviewer did not see; reconciliation is too late for a payment.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the agent only prepared a noncommittal draft and no tool could write or submit it, stale binding would be a review-quality issue rather than an execution gate.
Details.transfer: Bind approval to exact action and state, then revalidate at the side-effect boundary and reapprove after mutation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Session intent does not authorize changed financial parameters or invoice state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A session approval plus latest-record execution can silently change the reviewed action.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Reconciliation after payment cannot undo an unauthorized or incorrect transfer.

items.prompt: A high-value payment requires a requester and an independent approver. The requester is also the only person currently receiving approval prompts, and the agent can see both identities in the same session. Select TWO: Which controls are required for this payment?
constraints: Role assignments, payment parameters, approval logs, and the organization’s separation-of-duties rule are available; the payment action has not executed.

options.text: Pause the payment, route the exact parameters to an independent approver, and record requester and approver identities separately.
Accept the requester’s confirmation because the parameters are displayed and the agent cannot alter them.
Send a second approval prompt to the same requester and treat the two confirmations as independent.
Execute only after both role checks pass, with the approval event bound to the same reviewed payment parameters.
Execute first and ask an independent approver to review the payment record afterward.

feedback.Reason: Pause the payment, route the exact parameters to an independent approver, record requester and approver identities separately, and execute only after both role checks pass. The decisive constraint is Human confirmation is not sufficient when the same principal can request and approve the side effect; approval must be bound to an independent authorized role.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes agents pausing for human feedback at checkpoints or blockers and asking users when preference or intent cannot be safely inferred. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Pause the payment, route the exact parameters to an independent approver, record requester and approver identities separately, and execute only after both role checks pass.
Details.errorCorrection: Parameter visibility does not remove the self-approval conflict, and a compromised or mistaken requester can still authorize the side effect alone. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the action were a nonconsequential draft with no external write, one user confirmation could be proportionate under the existing checkpoint pattern.
Details.transfer: Bind confirmation to an independent authorized role whenever the action has a consequential external effect.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Parameter visibility does not remove the self-approval conflict or establish an independent role.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Two prompts to the same principal do not create separation of duties.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Post-execution review cannot authorize a high-value side effect that has already occurred.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Required control: Pause the payment, route the exact parameters to an independent approver, and record requester and approver identities separately.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Required control: Execute only after both role checks pass, with the approval event bound to the same reviewed payment parameters.

items.prompt: Reviewers override a model recommendation in 12% of consequential cases, but the override reasons mix model errors, policy changes, and user preferences. The team wants to turn every raw override into a prompt or training change immediately. Select TWO: Which steps make overrides useful evidence?
constraints: Override decisions, reviewer reasons, policy versions, source evidence, model outputs, and an adjudicator can be linked before any prompt or model change.

options.text: Treat every override as a model failure, retrain immediately, and use a lower override rate as the success metric.
Record each override with its reason, policy version, evidence, and reviewer role.
Discard override reasons after the case is resolved and monitor only the total override percentage.
Change the prompt for every override first, then classify the reasons if the rate does not improve.
Adjudicate the categories, feed only validated model-error cases into evaluation, and retain preference cases as policy or workflow input.

feedback.Reason: Record the override with reason, policy/version, evidence, and reviewer role, adjudicate the categories, feed only validated model-error cases into the evaluation and improvement loop, and retain unresolved preference cases as policy or workflow input. The decisive constraint is A human override is an outcome requiring interpretation, not a uniformly labeled model error; policy and preference changes must be separated from reproducible model failures before they drive iteration.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes agents pausing for human feedback at checkpoints or blockers and asking users when preference or intent cannot be safely inferred. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Record the override with reason, policy/version, evidence, and reviewer role, adjudicate the categories, feed only validated model-error cases into the evaluation and improvement loop, and retain unresolved preference cases as policy or workflow input.
Details.errorCorrection: It conflates changed policy and legitimate preference with model error and can optimize away necessary human judgment or make the model repeat an outdated decision. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every override had a validated error category and unchanged policy/reference, the categorized cases could enter the evaluation loop directly without a separate adjudication hold.
Details.transfer: Interpret human feedback by reason and version before converting it into a model or prompt change.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Policy changes and legitimate preferences are not uniformly model errors, so reducing the rate can erase necessary judgment.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A total rate cannot distinguish model failures from policy or preference and loses the evidence needed for iteration.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Immediate prompt changes contaminate diagnosis and can encode an outdated policy before reasons are adjudicated.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Required control: Record each override with its reason, policy version, evidence, and reviewer role.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Required control: Adjudicate the categories, feed only validated model-error cases into evaluation, and retain preference cases as policy or workflow input.
